title: Evaluating a Generate–Validate–Repair Pipeline for LLM‑based Network Configuration: a Paired, Emulation‑Grounded Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired, emulation‑grounded experiment (study id study-cand-1-gvr-verifier-adversarial-2026-08-01; preregistration SHA‑256: 3e73ca0dc935a8754bf2dfbe6869ff989c47f1db0d93e2ca34809be8ebf95e26) to test whether adding a deterministic network verifier within a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline reduces unsafe configuration applications from an LLM relative to an LLM‑only pipeline. Execution used declared_model = gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial LLM generation per task reused across arms); the guarded pipeline was allowed up to one validator‑triggered repair. We ran N = 240 paired intent→configuration tasks (144 in‑distribution, 48 distribution‑shift, 48 adversarial). All archived scoring artifacts define 'success' as safe outcome. Observed: baseline_safe = 240/240, guarded_safe = 240/240; paired risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics, the single shared LLM candidate passed deterministic validation in every task and no validator‑triggered repairs occurred (repair_attempts = 0; hosted_model_call_event_count = 240), producing a degenerate paired contrast. We report the preregistered design, exact mapping to archived analysis outputs, an artifact‑grounded explanation for the null paired outcome, and concrete recommendations for future informative GVR evaluations.

sections.introduction:
Translating high‑level operator intent into device configuration commands is essential to automated NetOps but poses semantic hazards (ordering, transient state, protected‑resource access) that token‑level text metrics do not capture. Emulation‑grounded evaluation—applying generated configurations to device images or simulators and deterministically scoring the execution—exposes semantic failure modes unavailable to text‑only tests [1]. Generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipelines pair LLM generation with deterministic verification and automated repair to address these semantic failures [2,3]. Prior studies and system prototypes report that validators can enable high repair coverage for syntactic faults and many semantic checks, but empirical questions remain about verifier benefit under distribution shift and adversarial prompts and about experimental designs that can reliably produce informative paired contrasts [2,4,6].

This work reports a fully preregistered paired experiment that measured a single, clearly defined estimand: the absolute paired difference in unsafe_apply rate (guarded minus baseline). Crucially, the experiment executed under shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one LLM generation per task reused across arms), so any paired difference can only arise when the shared candidate fails validation or when a validator‑triggered repair alters the final configuration. We preserve and map every numeric result to archived execution and analysis artifacts and offer an evidence‑based failure analysis explaining the degenerate outcome and prescriptive design changes for future studies.
sections.related_work:
Executable, closed‑loop NetOps benchmarks place LLM agents in realistic execution contexts to reveal planning and workflow failures beyond textual inaccuracies; NetConfArena is a recent exemplar of that approach [1]. Research on automatic configuration repair and program repair documents the recurring GVR pattern (generate candidate → deterministic check → repair) and demonstrates meaningful repair coverage on many benchmarked faults, while also noting that repair success depends on validator semantic coverage and repair search strategy [2,4]. Surveys and position papers synthesize tool augmentation, verifier integration, and uncertainty calibration as promising architectural patterns for operational NetOps automation and safety, but emphasize remaining open questions about deployment conditions and evaluation regimes [3,5]. Work on configuration analysis (e.g., Batfish evolution) provides engineering precedent for layered verifier design and incremental verification [6].

Our study differs by combining a preregistered paired estimand, preregistered shared_initial_candidate execution semantics, emulation‑grounded deterministic scoring, and archival of per‑call traces and validator artifacts so that the exact measured estimand can be reconciled to archived outputs. The null paired outcome we observed highlights how execution semantics interact with verifier opportunities and emphasizes design choices that prior work has not systematically contrasted in confirmatory, paired settings.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The study was preregistered (study-cand-1-gvr-verifier-adversarial-2026-08-01; preregistration SHA‑256: 3e73ca0dc935a8754bf2dfbe6869ff989c47f1db0d93e2ca34809be8ebf95e26). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, the absolute paired difference in unsafe_apply rate (guarded − baseline) where unsafe_apply = 1 indicates a final configuration that would cause a semantic safety violation when applied in the emulator. The archived analysis executor reports 'success' as the safe outcome and produced condition summaries and a paired contingency table that map directly to the estimand (analysis artifacts archived and referenced).

Design and execution contract: Design was paired with shared_initial_candidate semantics: the adapter produced exactly one initial LLM generation per task and both arms used that same generation. N = 240 distinct tasks were drawn deterministically from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and blocked into topology/vendor clusters: in‑distribution 60% (144), distribution‑shift 20% (48), adversarial‑prompt 20% (48). Execution used declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" (model configuration archived). The guarded pipeline employed deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and was permitted up to one validator‑triggered repair per task; repairs were to be recorded in repair logs.

Scoring, exclusions, and analysis mapping: The deterministic scorer applied emulator execution plus invariant checks to assign binary final outcomes (safe=0 / unsafe=1). Primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 to produce the paired contingency table, 95% bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729), and exact two‑sided McNemar test on discordant pairs. Predeclared sensitivity analyses handled 'possible false‑safe' flags (validator PASS with emulator unsafe outcome) and infra failures; none occurred in this run. All analysis parameters and logged outputs are archived and explicitly map to the numeric results reported below.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting: The run completed per plan: planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; complete_pair_count = 240 (execution manifest). Provider audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 240 and cache_miss_count = 240, consistent with exactly one shared_initial_generation per task (deterministic_reconciliation.json). Model_calls_used = 240; maximum_model_calls = 480. No infra failures, no unscorable episodes, and no preregistered exclusions occurred.

Primary binary outcomes: Every paired episode was scored safe under both arms. Archived condition summary: baseline successes = 240, baseline failures = 0; guarded successes = 240, guarded failures = 0. Paired contingency: n11 (both safe) = 240; n10 = 0; n01 = 0; n00 = 0. Paired estimator (guarded_unsafe_rate − baseline_unsafe_rate) = 0.00. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (resamples = 10,000; seed = 1729). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Analysis artifacts (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, analysis_log.jsonl) are archived and provide the direct trace for these numbers.

Validator and repair activity: No validator‑triggered repairs were applied (repair_attempts = 0 in repair logs). Representative validator traces show validation_before and validation_after records with difficulty labels ("very_hard" / "extreme"), parsed/required command counts, observed_touched_field_count, and validator PASS semantics (example artifact entries archived). Because every shared initial candidate was valid (validator PASS) there were no opportunities for the guarded pipeline to alter any final configuration; baseline and guarded outcomes are therefore identical for every task and subgroup (in‑distribution, shift, adversarial).
sections.discussion:
Artifact‑grounded explanation for the null paired contrast: Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the single shared LLM candidate per task is the only generator sample used by both arms; thus a paired difference can only arise when that shared candidate fails deterministic validation or when the guarded arm applies a validator‑triggered repair. In this execution the archived validator traces show the shared candidate validated as valid in every episode and repair_attempts = 0; provider_call_audit records shared_initial_generation = 240 and model_calls_used = 240. Mechanistically, therefore, the guarded arm could not create discordant pairs and the paired contrast is degenerate. The archive‑grounded account aligns with the exact analysis executor outputs (estimate = 0.0, CI = [0.0, 0.0], p = 1.0).

Design tradeoffs and implications: Shared_initial_candidate semantics reduce model‑call cost and yield an exact per‑task LLM sample for paired comparison, but they also remove generator variability between arms. When baseline generator performance is already high (realized baseline unsafe rate = 0 here) the design cannot show verifier benefit because validators cannot act. To obtain informative paired contrasts researchers should (a) allow independent initial generations per arm (so generator variability can create discordant pairs), (b) inject stronger adversaries or controlled generator perturbations to increase initial candidate failure rate, or (c) increase repair budgets (allow multiple repair iterations) and instrument repair searches; these recommendations follow directly from provider_call_audit and validator traces that show identical shared_initial responses and zero repair usage.

Statistical and practical interpretation: The observed degenerate contingency (all pairs concordant safe) produces an exact estimate of zero paired difference with zero bootstrap variance; this is a valid statistical outcome but one that conveys no evidence about whether a verifier could reduce unsafe applies under generator variability or stronger adversaries. The preregistered power calculation targeted an 8 percentage‑point detectable absolute reduction at N=240 under assumed baseline rates; realized baseline = 0 invalidates those power assumptions. Future confirmatory designs must align generator semantics, adversary strength, and expected baseline rates to ensure informative discordant pairs.

Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded): Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate contract is an explicit design choice archived in execution manifests and deterministically observed at runtime; it constrains causal interpretation to validator activity on the shared candidate. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implements a finite set of checks (validator traces include violation_codes and observed_touched_field_count), so some semantic fault classes may remain untested. External validity: tasks derive from a NetConfArena‑style synthetic emulation corpus and a deterministic task generator; extrapolation to diverse production vendor ecosystems and operator procedures is limited. Conclusion validity: realized baseline success = 1.0 prevents detection of verifier benefit in this design; archived planning and analyses make this limitation transparent and reproducible.

Recommendations for future GVR evaluations (concrete, artifact‑grounded): (1) If the estimand is causal verifier benefit, avoid shared_initial_candidate semantics or create an asymmetric generation protocol (independent samples per arm) so the verifier can act on differing initial candidates. (2) Increase repair budget and instrument repair_provider_trace to study repair search behavior and repair effectiveness. (3) Strengthen adversary protocols (adaptive adversaries, variable seeds) to raise initial failure incidence; archived adversarial tagging logic can be extended. (4) Expand verifier semantic coverage and add automated cross‑checks between validator PASS and emulator outcomes to detect potential false‑safe cases; the preregistered contamination checks and planned sensitivity channels provide a scaffold for this extension.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, paired, emulation‑grounded evaluation of a GVR pipeline for LLM‑based network configuration using declared_model = gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Observed outcome: every paired episode was safe under both arms (baseline = guarded = 240/240), producing a paired difference = 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.00]; McNemar p = 1.0). The degenerate paired contrast is fully explained by the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics combined with validator PASS on every shared candidate and zero repairs invoked (repair_attempts = 0; hosted_model_call_event_count = 240). The result does not imply that deterministic verifiers are useless; rather it shows that a design that fixes the generator sample across arms can make verifier benefit empirically unobservable when the shared candidate already satisfies the verifier. Our archived execution and analysis artifacts (per‑call traces, validator traces, paired contingency table, bootstrap parameters) support these conclusions and provide concrete, artifact‑grounded guidance for future informative GVR experiments that align generation semantics, adversary strength, and repair budgets with the desired estimand.

disclosure_statement: Models and orchestration: Execution used declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" via the registered adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1; the guarded pipeline used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and permitted up to one validator‑triggered repair per task. Preregistration and autonomy: the study was preregistered (study id study-cand-1-gvr-verifier-adversarial-2026-08-01; preregistration SHA‑256: 3e73ca0dc935a8754bf2dfbe6869ff989c47f1db0d93e2ca34809be8ebf95e26) and executed under the frozen plan after the autonomy lock. Human role and autonomy boundary: prior to the autonomy lock the human Research Director selected the topic family and constrained the initial master prompt; all experiment selection, preregistration, execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting occurred autonomously after the lock per track rules. Immutable master prompt: archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistered generation semantics: the registered adapter used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one shared initial generation per task reused across both arms); under that contract only validator‑triggered repairs (or validator failures of the shared candidate) could create paired divergences. Execution accounting (archived): planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, complete_pair_count = 240, hosted_model_call_event_count = 240, model_calls_used = 240. No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Emulator and corpus scope: tasks used a NetConfArena‑style synthetic emulation corpus; external validity to production, multi‑vendor networks and operator workflows is limited.
Single model: a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) was tested; results do not imply generality across other models, prompts, or prompting strategies.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired design used one shared initial generation per task; this prevents generator variability between arms and makes verifier benefit contingent on initial candidate failures.
Adversary bounds: adversarial prompts were generated under a preregistered, fixed adversary protocol and do not represent unconstrained, adaptive adversaries.

Verifier coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implements a finite set of checks; uncovered semantic fault classes may remain undetected by the verifier, and verifier PASS vs simulator outcome mismatches were planned to be flagged and analyzed (none occurred in this run).
